insights.insight: The protocol holds 11,270 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — confirmed transactions, not inferred intent. At a time when the ad industry charges $5+ CPM for probabilistic targeting, this is a structurally different class of signal.

At $936K cumulative GMV and a 7-day run rate of $183K, the network crosses $1M in approximately 2-3 days — driven by compounding velocity (1.03x) and acceleration (1.003x) both above 1.0x simultaneously, not a spike.

insights.topic: Category diversity is expanding, not concentrating
insights.insight: Category entropy at 3.236 bits indicates no single category dominates the receipt pool; grocery, fuel, dining, hardware, warehouse, and — as of April 9 — SaaS subscriptions are all represented, making this dataset useful across verticals.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion pattern signals organic growth
insights.insight: The network expands in documented pulse-then-quiet cycles — 14 new CBSAs in one heartbeat (rural OH, CA, ID, NE, IA), followed by only 2 the next — a rhythm consistent with social graph propagation rather than paid acquisition, which affects signal quality assessments.

Spend tokens carry no wallet reference in the signed payload, meaning purchase signals are identity-free at the individual level — aggregate verified commerce data without the regulatory and consent exposure that comes with cookie-based or device-graph targeting.

insights.topic: Competitive default: participate or be analyzed anyway
insights.insight: The protocol's data flywheel accumulates verified purchase signals regardless of brand participation — each new receipt increases the analytical value of all prior signals. Brands that delay cede first-mover access to their own category data.
